newsitem.title: ITALY: Groundstaff strike to hit Milan airports on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Groundstaff strike to hit Milan airports on Friday.

text.p: A general strike called by groundstaff unions at Milan's Linate and Malpensa airports for Friday from 0900 to 1300 GMT could cause flight delays or cancellations, the airports' management company said.

SEA-Aeroporti di Milan said in a statement that the strike was linked to plans to transfer personnel from Linate, just outside Milan's eastern edge to Malpensa, about 40 km northwest of the city, in 1998.
"Difficulties for passengers will be inevitable," its statement said.
Linate, used for short-haul flights, has reached capacity, has no space to expand and cannot handle large wide-bodied aircraft.
A two trillion lire capital improvement programme, called Malpensa 2000, is underway to consolidate all international and most domestic operations at the airport.

On completion of the first phase of the project in 1998, SEA will transfer all international and some domestic traffic from Linate. Malpensa will then take 80 percent of Milan air passenger traffic and 90 percent of cargo.
